entities.name: PMID:25071375
observations: In male Wistar-Kyoto rats with nephrotoxic serum nephritis, sirolimus monotherapy was given at 0.25 mg/kg/day subcutaneously from day 1 to day 14.
Sirolimus reduced selected glomerular and tubulointerstitial injury measures but did not significantly improve crescent formation, macrophage accumulation, or proteinuria progression.

entities.name: Sirolimus
observations: In nephrotoxic serum nephritis rats, induction monotherapy reduced kidney enlargement by 41%, improved endogenous creatinine clearance by 50%, and reduced glomerular and tubulointerstitial cell proliferation by 53% and 70%, respectively; reported P<0.05.

Sirolimus reduced segmental fibrinoid necrosis by 69%, autologous rat IgG deposition, glomerular tuft enlargement, periglomerular myofibroblast accumulation, and multiple tubulointerstitial injury markers; reported P<0.05.
Proteinuria progression, crescent formation, and macrophage accumulation were not significantly reduced.

entities.name: Nephrotoxic serum nephritis
observations: Rat model induced by sheep anti-rat glomerular basement membrane serum; vehicle-controlled comparison evaluated sirolimus induction monotherapy over 14 days.

entities.name: Selected renal protection
observations: Sirolimus monotherapy produced significant but incomplete protection: benefits were observed in several glomerular and tubulointerstitial measures, with more consistent histological protection in the tubulointerstitium than in glomeruli.
The result supports the wording 'selected beneficial effects' rather than comprehensive suppression of nephritic injury.
